title: Fluency and real calls
lead: Final week. Is lesson ke baad tum poora client call structure kar paoge: summarize, main point, next step, schedule, aur polite close.
description: Week 12 English lesson: summarize a call, confirm action items, schedule the next step, and close with confidence.

patterns.note: Call ke end me points short me repeat karo.
patterns.say: Let me summarize the main points.
patterns.positive: Let me summarize the main points.
patterns.negative: I don't have a full summary yet.
patterns.question: Can you summarize the call?
examples: Let me summarize what we decided.
Main summarize karta hoon kya decide hua.
Let me summarize the three action items.
Main teen action items summarize karta hoon.
patterns.grammar: Let me + base verb. summarize = short me repeat karna. Summary me 2–3 points, not story.
patterns.mistake: “Let me to summarize” → “Let me summarize.” let me ke baad base verb.

patterns.say: The main point is the deadline.
patterns.positive: The main point is the deadline.
patterns.negative: The main point isn't the price.
patterns.question: What is the main point?
examples: The main point is the launch date.
Main point launch date hai.
The main point is the client's approval.
Main point client ki approval hai.
patterns.grammar: The main point is + noun/clause. Ek point, five nahi.
patterns.mistake: “The main point is about the deadline” → “The main point is the deadline.” Direct noun better.

patterns.note: Call close karne se pehle last item.
patterns.say: Before we finish, let's confirm the next call.
patterns.positive: Before we finish, let's confirm the next call.
patterns.negative: Before we finish, let's not forget the payment question.
patterns.question: Before we finish, can we confirm the date?
examples: Before we finish, I have one question.
Finish karne se pehle, ek sawaal hai.
Before we finish, let's agree on the next step.
Finish se pehle next step par agree karein.
patterns.grammar: Before + subject + verb, + main clause. before we finish = call end hone se pehle.
patterns.mistake: “Before finish, let's confirm” → “Before we finish, let's confirm.” Subject chahiye.

patterns.note: Call ke baad kaam ka owner bolo.
patterns.say: I'll follow up with the client tomorrow.
patterns.positive: I'll follow up with the client tomorrow.
patterns.negative: I won't follow up until Monday.
patterns.question: Who will follow up?
examples: I'll follow up with the design team.
Main design team se follow up karunga.
I'll follow up on the invoice.
Main invoice par follow up karunga.
patterns.grammar: follow up with + person; follow up on + topic. Future promise.
patterns.mistake: “I'll follow up to the client” → “I'll follow up with the client.” with person.

patterns.note: Next call ka time set karo.
patterns.say: Could we schedule the next call for Monday?
patterns.positive: Could we schedule the next call for Monday?
patterns.negative: We can't schedule it this week.
patterns.question: Could we schedule a call?
examples: Could we schedule a demo for Thursday?
Kya hum Thursday ke liye demo schedule kar sakte hain?
Could we schedule the review for next week?
Kya hum review next week ke liye rakh sakte hain?
patterns.grammar: Could we + base verb. schedule something for + time.
patterns.mistake: “Could we schedule to Monday?” → “Could we schedule it for Monday?” for + time.

patterns.note: Call close karne ki simple, professional line.
patterns.negative: I don't want to take more of your time.
patterns.question: Do you have five more minutes?
examples: Thanks for your time. I'll send the notes.
Aapke time ke liye thanks. Main notes bhej doonga.
Thanks for your time today.
Aaj ke time ke liye thanks.
patterns.grammar: Thanks for + noun/-ing. Call close karne ka polite line. time uncountable.
patterns.mistake: “Thanks for your times” → “Thanks for your time.” Time uncountable.

dialogue.context: Final mock client call. Riya = client. Summary, next step, schedule aur close — poora structure.

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.text: Okay, I think we have covered everything.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Let me summarize. The main point is the launch date — the 15th.

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.text: Yes, and we need the content by the 10th.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Correct. Before we finish, let's confirm the next call.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: That works. Could we schedule it for Monday at four?

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.text: Sure. Can you send the notes?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes, I'll follow up with the notes today. Thanks for your time.

dialogue.closing: Poora call: open → discuss → summarize → next step → schedule → thanks. Ye structure roz use karo.

speakPrompts.title: 1. Summarize
speakPrompts.prompt: Call ke teen points summarize karo.
speakPrompts.starter: Let me summarize. The main point is ___ . We also agreed on ___ .

speakPrompts.title: 2. Confirm action items
speakPrompts.starter: I'll follow up with ___ . You will send ___ by ___ .

speakPrompts.title: 3. Schedule next call
speakPrompts.starter: Could we schedule the next call for ___ ? Does that work for you?

speakPrompts.title: 4. Full 2-minute call
speakPrompts.starter: Hi, thanks for joining. Let's start with ___ . ... Let me summarize. ... Thanks for your time.

vocab.example: Let me give you a quick summary.

selfCheck: Call ko “Let me summarize” se close kiya.

pronunciation.title: Pausing
pronunciation.body: Let me summarize — the main point is — the deadline. Pause se listener ko process karne ka time milta hai.

pronunciation.title: Rhythm
pronunciation.body: Content words par stress: LET me SUMmarize the MAIN POINT. Function words halke.

pronunciation.title: Final intonation
pronunciation.body: Statements me voice neeche. “Thanks for your time.” — end me confident fall.

pronunciation.title: Confidence
pronunciation.body: Speed slow rakho. Bhool gaye to “Let me check that and follow up” bolo — pause se better hai.
